name: Michigan

rule.hpNote: motor more than 6 hp (PWC: anyone born after Dec. 31, 1978)
rule.textEn: Anyone born on or after July 1, 1996 needs a boating safety certificate to run a motorboat over 6 hp; for a PWC the certificate is needed by anyone born after Dec. 31, 1978.
rule.textEs: Quien nació el 1 de julio de 1996 o después necesita un certificado de seguridad náutica para manejar una lancha de más de 6 hp; para una moto acuática lo necesita toda persona nacida después del 31 de diciembre de 1978.

minAge.note: Under 12: up to 6 hp freely; over 6 and up to 35 hp only with a certificate and a supervisor 16+ on board; never over 35 hp. PWC: none under 14; 14-15 with a certificate and an adult 21+ on board or within 100 ft; alone from 16 with a certificate.

exemptions: People born before July 1, 1996 (motorboats) or on/before Dec. 31, 1978 (PWC).

card.feeNote: Copies are reprinted through the DNR eLicense system; course providers may charge fees.

pwcExtra: PWC: no one under 14; ages 14-15 need a certificate plus a parent, guardian or designated adult 21+ on board or operating a PWC within 100 ft; independent operation from 16 with a certificate.

sources.quote: a boating safety certificate (or boater education card) is required for anyone born on or after July 1, 1996, who operates a vessel.
May operate a boat with a motor more than 6 horsepower only if they possess boating safety certificate.
No certificate required: Only if born on or before Dec. 31, 1978
More than 35 horsepower: May not operate under any circumstances.
Are directly supervised on board by someone at least 16 years old.
Not allowed to operate a personal watercraft under any circumstances.
Minimum age to operate independently: 16 (with certificate)
Approved online courses allow you to study at your own pace from home using electronic materials and videos.
Recreational safety certificate requests are only processed online through eLicense.
